answer.label: Written by
answer.sourceLine: This is the opening of Dickinson’s short poem “Dawn,” published posthumously in Poems: Third Series (1896); the manuscript (Fr1647B) is a fair copy Dickinson made around 1884.

source.heading: The source
source.excerpt:
Not knowing when the dawn will come
I open every door;
Or has it feathers like a bird,
Or billows like a shore?
trail: Written in pencil as a fair copy around 1884; the manuscript is catalogued as Franklin 1647B and held among Dickinson's papers.
First appeared in print a decade after Dickinson's death, as poem VII (titled “Dawn”) in Poems: Third Series (1896) ↗, edited by Mabel Loomis Todd.
Later reprinted under its first line as the title in The Complete Poems of Emily Dickinson (1924) ↗.
The poem is also documented in Dickinson's correspondence with editor Thomas Wentworth Higginson, cataloged as Johnson poem 1619 ↗.

source.rightsNote: “Dawn” was first published in 1896, and Dickinson died in 1886 — both well before the 1931 U.S. public-domain cutoff, so the poem is in the public domain in the United States.

author.name: Emily Dickinson
author.heading: About Emily Dickinson
author.bio: Emily Dickinson wrote nearly 1,800 poems in near-total seclusion in Amherst, Massachusetts, almost none of which were published in her lifetime. Her family and an editor, Mabel Loomis Todd, brought her work to print after her death, and she is now regarded as one of the most original voices in American poetry.
